primaryText: John broke the vase entails John did something.
translation: John broke the vase entails John did something.
comment: The feature attribution follows §4's account of own-energy action; the paper attributes none here.

primaryText: The vase broke does not entail The vase did something.
translation: The vase broke does not entail The vase did something.
comment: A happen-clause: no feature.

primaryText: John broke the vase: it therefore follows that he did something.
translation: John broke the vase: it therefore follows that he did something.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (7).

primaryText: The vase broke: therefore it did something.
translation: The vase broke: therefore it did something.

primaryText: John marched the prisoners entails The prisoners did something.
translation: John marched the prisoners entails The prisoners did something.
comment: The entailment form detects the agentive object, which the what-X-did form does not; the attribution follows the denial of the object's agentivity in (64).

primaryText: John shot the prisoners does not entail The prisoners did something.
translation: John shot the prisoners does not entail The prisoners did something.

primaryText: What the wind did was blow the tree down.
translation: What the wind did was blow the tree down.
comment: A natural agent is a doer; the attribution follows §4, where the wind of (56) is a true agentive, while here the paper says only that such nouns are perhaps grammatically animate.

primaryText: What happened to the wind was that it blew the tree down.
translation: What happened to the wind was that it blew the tree down.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (13).

primaryText: What the computer is doing is calculating the correlation coefficient.
translation: What the computer is doing is calculating the correlation coefficient.
comment: Certain machines use their own energy (§4); the attribution is inferred.

primaryText: What is happening to the computer is that it is calculating the correlation coefficient.
translation: What is happening to the computer is that it is calculating the correlation coefficient.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (15).

primaryText: The bullet smashed John's collar-bone.
translation: The bullet smashed John's collar-bone.
comment: An indisputably inanimate doer, by its kinetic energy; the attribution follows §2's force from motion, and is inferred.

primaryText: What the bullet did was smash John's collar-bone.
translation: What the bullet did was smash John's collar-bone.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (17).

primaryText: What happened to the bullet was that it smashed John's collar-bone.
translation: What happened to the bullet was that it smashed John's collar-bone.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (17).

primaryText: A: Why does the door do that? B: What? A: Fly open every time the wind blows.
translation: A: Why does the door do that? B: What? A: Fly open every time the wind blows.
comment: The difference between do and happen is neutralized, do being the normal form; the circumstances are left open.

primaryText: A: Why does the vase do that? B: What? A: Keep falling off the shelf.
translation: A: Why does the vase do that? B: What? A: Keep falling off the shelf.
comment: Neutralization of do and happen.

primaryText: A: Why does that happen to the door? B: What? A: Why does it fly open every time the wind blows?
translation: A: Why does that happen to the door? B: What? A: Why does it fly open every time the wind blows?
comment: Not deviant in any radical way, but artificial; entered as marginal.

primaryText: Christ died in order to save us from our sins.
translation: Christ died in order to save us from our sins.
comment: A process verb with a do-interpretation.

primaryText: What Christ did was die in order to save us from our sins.
translation: What Christ did was die in order to save us from our sins.

primaryText: What happened to Christ was that he died in order to save us from our sins.
translation: What happened to Christ was that he died in order to save us from our sins.

primaryText: What John is doing is standing/sitting/lying in the middle of the room.
translation: What John is doing is standing/sitting/lying in the middle of the room.
comment: Stand, sit and lie refer to states yet are do-verbs; no feature is attributed in the paper.

primaryText: What I did was have my passport ready.
translation: What I did was have my passport ready.
comment: A do-interpretation where the progressive is impossible.

primaryText: I am having my passport ready.
translation: I am having my passport ready.

primaryText: What you must do is be absent that day.
translation: What you must do is be absent that day.

primaryText: You are being absent.
translation: You are being absent.

primaryText: What John did was drift two miles further down the river, so as to avoid landing in enemy territory.
translation: What John did was drift two miles further down the river, so as to avoid landing in enemy territory.
comment: An act of will without own energy: the do-feature is due entirely to the volitive feature.

primaryText: What John did was not eat anything for two days.
translation: What John did was not eat anything for two days.

primaryText: What John did was be ready.
translation: What John did was be ready.
comment: Willing a state is a kind of doing.

primaryText: What John did was not sleep that night, so as to forestall any surprise attack.
translation: What John did was not sleep that night, so as to forestall any surprise attack.

primaryText: What happened to John was that he did not sleep that night, so as to forestall any surprise attack.
translation: What happened to John was that he did not sleep that night, so as to forestall any surprise attack.

primaryText: What John did was not sleep that night, through no fault of his own.
translation: What John did was not sleep that night, through no fault of his own.
comment: With volition denied, the clause becomes a happen-clause.

primaryText: What happened to John was that he did not sleep that night, through no fault of his own.
translation: What happened to John was that he did not sleep that night, through no fault of his own.

primaryText: What John did was die in a car accident.
translation: What John did was die in a car accident.
comment: Dying without an act of will, unlike (24).

primaryText: What happened to John was that he died in a car accident.
translation: What happened to John was that he died in a car accident.

primaryText: John accidentally trod on the toy, in order to punish the child.
translation: John accidentally trod on the toy, in order to punish the child.
comment: The purpose phrase tests volitivity; the agentivity of the noun is irrelevant.

primaryText: What John did was kick the bucket over accidentally.
translation: What John did was kick the bucket over accidentally.
comment: A do-sentence without volition; that the remaining feature is the agentive is inferred.

primaryText: Kick the bucket over accidentally!
translation: Kick the bucket over accidentally!
comment: The imperative tests volitivity, not the do-relation; the attribution is inferred as for (41).

primaryText: What John did was sneeze.
translation: What John did was sneeze.
comment: A do-sentence Anderson counts as non-ergative, his ergative being volitive plus agentive; the attribution of the agentive alone is inferred.

primaryText: What happened to John was that he sneezed.
translation: What happened to John was that he sneezed.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (43).

primaryText: What John did was cry.
translation: What John did was cry.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (43).

primaryText: What happened to John was that he cried.
translation: What happened to John was that he cried.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (43).

primaryText: John carefully fell out of the window.
translation: John carefully fell out of the window.
comment: Carefully detects volitivity together with agentivity; that falling carries neither is inferred.

primaryText: John carefully and accidentally pushed the door open.
translation: John carefully and accidentally pushed the door open.
comment: That accidentally pushing carries the agentive without the volitive is inferred.

primaryText: John carefully pushed the door open.
translation: John carefully pushed the door open.

primaryText: These columns support the weight of the pediment.
translation: These columns support the weight of the pediment.
comment: Force from position: the effective feature.

primaryText: What these columns do is support the weight of the pediment.
translation: What these columns do is support the weight of the pediment.
comment: Printed as 'What these column do'.

primaryText: What happens to these columns is that they support the weight of the pediment.
translation: What happens to these columns is that they support the weight of the pediment.

primaryText: The flying stone broke the window.
translation: The flying stone broke the window.
comment: Force from motion: the effective feature.

primaryText: What the flying stone did was break the window.
translation: What the flying stone did was break the window.

primaryText: What happened to the flying stone was that it broke the window.
translation: What happened to the flying stone was that it broke the window.

primaryText: The wind opened the door.
translation: The wind opened the door.
comment: Fillmore's instrumental; for Cruse the wind is a true agentive in a do-relationship with opened.

primaryText: The stone broke the window.
translation: The stone broke the window.
comment: Ambiguous between the instrumental reading of (58) and the effective reading of (60); a do-sentence only under the second.

primaryText: John broke the window with a stone.
translation: John broke the window with a stone.
comment: The stone is an instrumental, not in a do-relationship with broke.

primaryText: John broke the window with the stone: it therefore follows that the stone did something.
translation: John broke the window with the stone: it therefore follows that the stone did something.

primaryText: As a result of the explosion, a stone flew across the road and broke the window.
translation: As a result of the explosion, a stone flew across the road and broke the window.
comment: The context selecting the effective reading of (57).

primaryText: This key will open the door.
translation: This key will open the door.
comment: The instrumental reading is dominant.

primaryText: The warder marched the prisoners across the yard.
translation: The warder marched the prisoners across the yard.
comment: Initiation of an action by giving a command.

primaryText: John galloped the horse around the field.
translation: John galloped the horse around the field.

primaryText: John galloped the horse, which had died the previous day, round the field.
translation: John galloped the horse, which had died the previous day, round the field.
comment: The context denies the agentivity of the object.

primaryText: John galloped the horse, with which he had no means of communicating, around the field.
translation: John galloped the horse, with which he had no means of communicating, around the field.
comment: The context denies a channel of communication between subject and object.

primaryText: The warder marched the prisoners, who were successfully resisting any form of persuasion or command, across the yard.
translation: The warder marched the prisoners, who were successfully resisting any form of persuasion or command, across the yard.
comment: The context denies the responsiveness of the object to command.

primaryText: John moved (himself) to avoid the falling stones.
translation: John moved (himself) to avoid the falling stones.
comment: Reflexivization of an ergative verb has minor semantic effects when the agentive feature is present.

primaryText: The machine automatically switches (itself) off at 6 p.m.
translation: The machine automatically switches (itself) off at 6 p.m.

primaryText: The fire rapidly spread (itself) through the building.
translation: The fire rapidly spread (itself) through the building.
comment: A natural agent as the subject of an intransitive.

primaryText: Every year, the sea, by constantly eating away at the shore, inched (itself) closer to the village.
translation: Every year, the sea, by constantly eating away at the shore, inched (itself) closer to the village.

primaryText: The stone flew through the air.
translation: The stone flew through the air.
comment: The paper says only that the agentive feature is absent; no feature is entered.

primaryText: The stone flew itself through the air.
translation: The stone flew itself through the air.
comment: Reflexivization has considerable effects when the agentive feature is absent; no feature is entered.

primaryText: The ball rolled across the floor.
translation: The ball rolled across the floor.
comment: The paper says only that the agentive feature is absent.

primaryText: The ball rolled itself across the floor.
translation: The ball rolled itself across the floor.
comment: By no means impossible, but suggests that the ball contained some sort of mechanism; entered as marginal, the binary judgment not expressing acceptability with a meaning change.

primaryText: John laughed himself sore.
translation: John laughed himself sore.
comment: A kind of reflexivization distinguishing non-ergative verbs carrying the feature.

primaryText: John shouted himself hoarse.
translation: John shouted himself hoarse.

primaryText: John fainted himself cold.
translation: John fainted himself cold.

primaryText: John fell himself flat.
translation: John fell himself flat.

primaryText: The stone flew.
translation: The stone flew.
comment: The paper says only that the stone is not capable of carrying the agentive feature; no feature is entered.

primaryText: The hawk flew.
translation: The hawk flew.
comment: Capable of carrying the agentive feature; the attribution to the sentence is inferred.

primaryText: The model aeroplane flew.
translation: The model aeroplane flew.
comment: Capable of carrying the agentive feature, as a machine; the attribution is inferred.

primaryText: John flew the stone.
translation: John flew the stone.
comment: Jump and fly take as object only what is capable of carrying the agentive feature; the locative use, John flew the Atlantic, is excepted.

primaryText: John flew the hawk.
translation: John flew the hawk.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (80).

primaryText: John flew the model aeroplane.
translation: John flew the model aeroplane.
comment: Attribution inferred as for (81).

primaryText: The machine crushed the bottle when it fell on it.
translation: The machine crushed the bottle when it fell on it.
comment: The modification selects the effective reading.

primaryText: The machine crushed the bottle when we switched it on.
translation: The machine crushed the bottle when we switched it on.
comment: The modification selects the agentive reading.

primaryText: John smashed the window when he fell against it.
translation: John smashed the window when he fell against it.
comment: The modification selects the effective reading.

primaryText: John smashed the window with a stone.
translation: John smashed the window with a stone.
comment: The modification selects the agentive reading.

primaryText: The machine powerfully crushed the bottle when we switched it on.
translation: The machine powerfully crushed the bottle when we switched it on.
comment: Manner adverbs of energy output discriminate effective from agentive.

primaryText: The machine powerfully crushed the bottle when it fell on it.
translation: The machine powerfully crushed the bottle when it fell on it.

primaryText: John vigorously smashed the window with a stone.
translation: John vigorously smashed the window with a stone.

primaryText: John vigorously smashed the window when he fell against it.
translation: John vigorously smashed the window when he fell against it.

primaryText: John vigorously looked at Mary.
translation: John vigorously looked at Mary.
comment: The adverbs are less satisfactory where physical action is not prominent; look may be the volitive rather than the agentive counterpart of see, so no feature is attributed.
